candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: deathPlace

Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: spatial

Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: location matches Event → Place (Road is a Place)

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: streetAddress
candidates.comment: A textual representation of the street address component of a postal address. Also called "address line", "house number and street", "road address". Examples: "The postal address has streetAddress 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy", "The streetAddress is Main Street 123", "This address includes a streetAddress component."

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: arrivalBusStop
candidates.comment: An arrival bus stop relation between a bus trip and the station or stop where it concludes. Also called destination bus stop, final bus station. Examples: "A bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Grand Central Station'.", "The bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Main Street Stop'."

candidates.label: countriesNotSupported
candidates.comment: A geographical restriction relation between a software application and the countries where it is not supported. Also called: unsupported regions, restricted countries, unavailable in. Examples: "App X" countries not supported "Cuba", "Software Y" countries not supported "Iran, North Korea", "Game Z" countries not supported "Syria". Distinct from countriesSupported, which lists where the application is supported.

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".

candidates.label: numberOfAirbags
candidates.comment: The number or type of airbags present in a vehicle. Also called airbag count, vehicle airbags, safety airbags. Examples: "Car X numberOfAirbags 6", "SUV Y numberOfAirbags '8 (front, side, curtain)'", "Truck Z numberOfAirbags 2".

candidates.label: meetsEmissionStandard
candidates.comment: An emission standard compliance relation between a vehicle and the qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the emission standard it meets. Also called: emission compliant, environmentally certified, low emission. Examples: "Electric Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Zero Emission'", "New Diesel Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Euro 6'", "Hybrid Vehicle meetsEmissionStandard 'CARB LEV III'".

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

chosen_property.label: haltedTrainService
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that a fire event caused a train service to be halted.

candidates.label: trainNumber
candidates.comment: A train number relation between a train trip and its unique identifier. Also called train ID, railway number, service number. Examples: "TrainTrip trainNumber 'TGV 9876'", "TrainTrip trainNumber 'Acela Express 2150'", "TrainTrip trainNumber 'IC 123'".

candidates.label: trainName
candidates.comment: A train name relation between a train trip and the specific name of the train. Also called name of train, railway name, train service name. Examples: "TrainTrip trainName 'The Orient Express'", "TrainTrip trainName 'Shinkansen Nozomi'", "TrainTrip trainName 'Eurostar'".

candidates.label: departurePlatform
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a train trip and the platform from which it departs. Also called: platform number, train platform, departure track. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure platform "Platform 5", "Commuter Train" departure platform "Track 3". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which is the arrival platform.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: arrivalStation
candidates.comment: A station where a train trip concludes. Also called: train destination, end station, terminal station. Examples: "TrainTrip 456 arrivalStation 'Grand Central Station'", "TrainTrip from Rome arrivalStation 'Termini Station'", "TrainTrip to Berlin arrivalStation 'Hauptbahnhof'". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which specifies the specific platform within a station.

candidates.label: arrivalPlatform
candidates.comment: A platform identification for a train trip's arrival location. Also called: train arrival platform, destination platform. Examples: "TrainTrip 123 arrivalPlatform 'Platform 7'", "TrainTrip to London arrivalPlatform 'Track 1'", "TrainTrip from Paris arrivalPlatform 'Gate C'."

candidates.label: departureBusStop
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: arrivalBusStop
candidates.comment: An arrival bus stop relation between a bus trip and the station or stop where it concludes. Also called destination bus stop, final bus station. Examples: "A bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Grand Central Station'.", "The bus trip's arrival bus stop is 'Main Street Stop'."
